new_statements.quote: p.554-555 §8.1: "Feminine nouns end in an unstressed -a in the singular direct case. [...] The case endings for the substantives are as follows: Direct Sing. m.: -ø, f.: -a (unstressed); Pl. m./f.: -e (stressed); Oblique Sing. m./f.: -e (stressed); Pl. m./f.: -ān (stressed)". p.565 §22.1.1: "The preterit endings in Dizi are: 1. -eym, 2. -ey, 3. -ø, 4. -eymān, 5. -eyrān, 6. -end with the accent falling on the last syllable of the stem; e.g., be-xót-eym 'I slept'". p.566 §24: "The imperfect is built with the past stem of the verb plus the imperfect marker -e and the preterit endings [...] with stress falling on the last syllable of the stem, e.g., az har ruja virít-e-ym". p.567 §27: "The perfect is built by the past participle of the verb with the stress falling on its last syllable".

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Read all 20 book pages (551-570) of from rendered page images (the scanned layer is unusable; pdf page N holds book pages 2N+549 and 2N+550). Identity: p. 551 states the sketch covers the sub-dialects of Karan, Lerd and Diz (Shahrud county) and Karnaq (Khoresh-e Rostam county), Khalkhal, with Karani as the model; these are four of Glottolog's eight kore1279 dialects (Karani, Lerd, Diz, Karnaq), so the languoid match is exact. Verbatim check of the quoted passages: p. 554 §8.1 "Feminine nouns end in an unstressed -a in the singular direct case... The case endings for the substantives are as follows:" and the p. 555 table (Direct sing. m. -ø, f. -a (unstressed); pl. m./f. -e (stressed); Obliq…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No general word-stress rule is stated. The source only marks stress morphologically: in nouns the feminine singular direct -a is unstressed while the plural/oblique endings -e and -ān are stressed (i.e. stress moves onto those endings); in past-tense verb forms (preterit in Dizi, imperfect, perfect, Lerdi progressive) stress falls on the last syllable of the past stem / past participle, before the person endings. This is consistent with a morphologically conditioned, ending-sensitive system (some suffixes stressed, person endings unstressed) as in other Tati varieties, but that generalisation is mine, not the author's.
new_statements.exceptions: Only that the feminine -a differs from the (stressed) case endings; sentence intonation (rising/falling/level) described separately in §6, p. 554.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level marking in a grammatical sketch of four village dialects (Karani as model, Lerdi, Dizi, Karnaqi), from 1950/1963/1965 fieldwork; verb statements are per tense; acute accent used sporadically in examples (virít-e-ym, be-xót-eym, bevrít-em, dalú-e).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog kore1279 'Karanic' = ISO okh 'Koresh-e Rostam', with dialects Diz, Gandomabi, Hezarrudi, Karani {Khoresh-e Rostam}, Karnaq, Kelasi, Lerd, Nowkiani. Yarshater 2009 describes exactly this group (Karani as model; Lerdi, Dizi in Shāhrud county; Karnaqi in Khoresh-e Rostam county), so the identity match is exact. The scan's named source (Stilo 1981) is a classification paper, not a description of this variety. Sister sources examined (Yarshater 1959 Shāhrudi = Shāl/Kolur; Yarshater 1960 and Asadi 2014 Kajali; Yarshater 1962 Ramandi) are other Tati languoids.

sources.note: Phonology (pp. 553-554: vowels, consonants, lengthening, gemination, assimilation, intonation) has no stress section and no general rule. Stress is mentioned only in the morphology: fem. sg. direct -a is unstressed while the case endings -e and -ān are stressed (p. 554-555 §8.1); Lerdi progressive present has the accent on the last syllable of the participle (p. 561-562 §19.1); Dizi preterit endings with the accent on the last syllable of the stem (p. 565 §22.1.1); imperfect with stress on the last syllable of the stem (p. 566 §24); perfect built on the past participle with stress on its last…

sources.note: Kajali, a sister gender-marking Khalkhal Tati dialect (Kāghazkonān district), not kore1279. Segmental inventory only; the word 'accent' occurs only in the sense 'dialect'; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Ramandi = Southern Tati (Eshtehardi, Takestani etc.), NOT kore1279. Says feminine nouns are marked by an unstressed -a 'with the stress regularly falling on the penultimate syllable, e.g. Esh. xoza'. Not usable for Karanic.
